name_note: GTDB places this species in the split genus Treponema_D; the genomes it contains and the published literature use the name Treponema succinifaciens.

sentences.text: A cross-sectional gut microbiome study of 1,801 women in Burkina Faso, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa reported loss of Treponema species in urban populations.
That study identified antibiotic susceptibility as a factor that might drive the absence of Treponema succinifaciens in urban populations.
Treponema succinifaciens was among gut taxa recovered from metagenomic analysis of the Iceman's internal tissues, carrying ancient DNA damage profiles.
Those taxa were reported to show high similarity to ancestral, non-Westernized human gut communities, providing a baseline for Copper Age intestinal ecosystems.
Trichuris trichiura and Strongyloides stercoralis infections have been reported to be associated with the expansion of Treponema succinifaciens.
